chunks: Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from Ibn Faḍḍāl, from Ibn Bukayr, who said:

I heard Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام saying: “Indeed, I take the dirham from one of you, while I am surely among the wealthiest of the people of al-Madīnah in possessions. I intend by that nothing except that you may be purified.”

key_terms.أَكْثَرِ: among the most abundant or wealthiest
key_terms.الدِّرْهَمَ: a dirham; a unit of money taken from the believers
key_terms.الْمَدِينَةِ: al-Madīnah, the city referred to in the narration

ai.seo_question: Why did Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام take money from his followers if he was already wealthy?
ai.summary: This hadith explains that when Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام takes wealth from his followers, it is not out of personal need despite his having considerable wealth. Rather, the purpose is their purification through fulfilling a financial duty tied to the Imam’s right.
